lines.en: label beachfive3:
scene sky

It’s Friday morning and, as previously agreed upon, I’m currently on my way to the Amamiya mansion to listen to whatever it is Ayane has to say regarding the state of our world and how immeasurably fucked up it is.

Granted, I’m sure a lot of it will just be me dejectedly agreeing to whatever she proposes since I really don’t care anymore...but maybe Makoto will miraculously start caring in my stead and balance her out?
Which is doubtful (as everything is doubtful) considering that Ayane has specifically informed me of just how little she seems to care, but there are crazier things that have happened.

Like, for example, have I ever told you about the time I was having sex with Maya on the roof only to have her disappear partway through? Because that was crazy, wasn’t it? Way crazier than whatever this is.

So yeah, today is going to be a day. And it will be a day that I do my best to not phone-in out of respect for the one girl I know who is doing a better job of keeping it together than everyone else combined.
scene black
So cheers to you, Ayane Amamiya — may your morning be full of joy and squandered opportunities to abandon a man who does not deserve you.
scene ayanepresentation1
: Lady and gentleman, I present to you...my foolproof plan to save the world and marry Sensei! Please be advised that the real title is still in progress and that this one is just a placeholder.
scene ayanepresentation2
: Did you really have to make shirts for us?
: Did you really have to wear one?
scene ayanepresentation3
: I wasn’t going to. But it looks good on me, doesn’t it?
: Yeah. Where are your glasses, though?
scene ayanepresentation4
: I’m actually wearing contacts today. Cool, right? And it only took me half an hour to put them in.
: I feel like that is significantly longer than such a thing is supposed to take.
: Hey! Stop flirting and pay attention to my plan to restore the world and everyone in it to the proper state!
scene ayanepresentation5
: Sorry, Ayane. It’s been a while since I’ve hung out with Makoto and I’ve forgotten the level of rude that I am supposed to be with her.
: Zero rude. You decided to be nice to me, remember? I think I’d actually prefer it if you’d bring that up to a four or five, though. It feels weird when you’re too nice.
: Shut up, Ayane is talking.
: Yeah, like that. That’s a good level.
: Are you two done now?
: Yeah, sorry.
scene ayanepresentation6
: Good! Then, let me begin by thanking both of you for coming and saying that I greatly appreciate you humoring me as my mind continues to be thrown into turmoil on a day-to-day basis!
: Amen.
scene ayanepresentation7

: Now, as you may already know, things have happened that have caused our world to reset near the end of every school year. What are these things, you ask? No clue! But what we do know is that it sucks!
: Do I need to raise my hand to disagree or can I just verbally do that right now?
: I think you just kind of did.
scene ayanepresentation8
: I continue to be surprised by just how okay with this you are when all it does is prevent you from ever achieving the future you’ve been working toward your entire life.
: I continue to be surprised by just how not okay with this you are when all this does is allow you to indefinitely have sex with a rapidly multiplying number of teenagers for the rest of eternity.
: And I continue to be ignored! Pay attention! I worked hard on this!
scene ayanepresentation9
: Sorry. But let the record show that I am right. And also that I think it would be okay if we’d take it a little easier in trying to uncover the secrets of a thing that defies all logic and science.
: Let the record also show that I have a photo of Makoto sucking a dildo backed up on my computer.
: Permission to strike the record, madam speaker?
scene ayanepresentation10
: Granted. Now, back to the topic at hand.
scene ayanepresentation11

: Right now, only three of us are aware of the state of the world: me, Sensei, and Makoto. And with Maya’s memories purged, we have no evidence that more than three people can safely know at any given time.
scene ayanepresentation12
: There have been instances in the past where that number has increased, but no evidence of such information carrying over from one timeline to the next as a value greater than three.
: Additionally, we’ve never had more than three people on the rooftop at once.
: And while this is in no way proof that such a thing is impossible, what it does do is provide a precedent and warning in regard to how we proceed from here.
scene ayanepresentation13
: What that means is even if we find someone with the ability to retain information about the loops, we have no guarantee that they’ll remember it once the next cycle begins...
: It also seems so far that this information is stored in a sort of...seniority-focused way. Maya was the first to know, followed by Sensei, then me, then Makoto.

: Once Makoto started retaining information and making it to the roof, Maya lost that ability. Which would mean, if that’s an indication of things to come, Sensei would be the next to go back to “normal.”
: Objection. I’d like to strike that from the record as well so Sensei doesn’t start blaming me for the disappearance of his beloved Maya.
: Denied. I’m not doing this to try and point fingers at anyone, I’m just saying that we need to be aware of the risks involved if we do start trying to tell other people about this.
scene ayanepresentation14
: It’s very possible that none of this is relevant at all. I just think it would be best if we didn’t get our hopes up since all that’s done in the past is let us down.
: As such, I think we need to accept that any one of us could be “gone” at any given moment. And, should that happen again, we can’t let ourselves fall into the state Sensei did after Maya.

: Our time is only infinite to a certain degree. And what we learned through Maya’s disappearance is that we need to cherish each and every single day we have together because we never know when our days will end.
scene ayanepresentation15
: Understood?
scene ayanepresentation16
: I’m sorry...to both of you. I wasn’t really thinking of that...I just didn’t know how to get out of bed.
: Way to go, Ayane. Your morbid message of “hope” has made Sensei upset.
: Sensei, you don’t have to apologize! I know exactly how hard this has been for you. But the reason we need to be careful about stuff like this is because we want to prevent it from happening again.
: So let this presentation be my promise that if you do vanish, I’ll keep working hard until I get you back. We’ve gotta keep the ball rolling or we’ll never get anywhere. Do you understand?
scene ayanepresentation17
: If this theory is true, though — this one based on “seniority,” we only have to experience it once more before pulling the plug on informing others, correct?
: Because Sensei being reset after one more new person makes it to the roof would establish a definitive pattern.
: And repeatedly cycling through three people over and over won’t give anyone a long enough time to really investigate anything. Right?
scene ayanepresentation18
: Right. Which is why I propose that we come up with a list of people who we think are both capable of maintaining a level head in the face of an apocalypse, as well as those we think are able to.
scene ayanepresentation19

: We already know that Maya, Yumi, and Tsuneyo are capable of knowing about the loops, but that’s the extent of our knowledge. And since I like to believe in everyone, I think they’d be able to remain strong.
: I’ve also included Miku and Sana in this list because of their respective connections to Makoto and I — and Nodoka and Noriko because they’re both really smart.
: I’m sure Noriko’s connection to Sensei counts for something as well. So if we’re going to tell anybody, I think these are the ones we need to stick to.

: You can go ahead and just remove Miku from that list now. I love her with all of my heart, but there’s no way she’d ever be able to comprehend any of this. And I know that for a fact because I’ve already tried.
: Actually...I’m glad you included Noriko on there. Because something she said the other day really got me thinking.
scene ayanepresentation20
: You guys already know that my memories got pretty messed up somewhere within the fifty-billion timelines we must’ve experienced, but they’ve been coming back little by little.
: Noriko mentioned that Maya might be in the same boat. Maybe her memories are just...locked away somewhere? Maybe something just needs to sort of...trigger them and remind her?
: With all due respect, Sensei, we don’t know for sure what caused your memories to fade. I’d argue that the effects of trauma are significantly more plausible than...timeline interference.
scene ayanepresentation21
: And I won’t argue against that. But if I need to be positive right now, I’m going to regurgitate the only bit of hope I’ve gotten since she vanished. And right now, that’s what I have.
: Maybe I’m wrong. In fact, I’m probably wrong.
: But, at the very least, it shows that Noriko is capable of picking up the differences in Maya’s behavior- and that seems to be something everyone else has struggled with.
: That’s actually another reason I included her.
scene ayanepresentation22
: Noriko told me about the talk you guys had and how you told her to come to me. That’s when I really started trying to throw this plan together.
: Well, what is the plan in the first place? Because I’m not sure if I’d call just doomsaying to all of our friends a concrete strategy.
: I’ll get to that in a second. I have to do more doomsaying first.
scene ayanepresentation23
: It’s been over six months since our last apocalypse.
: And while I’ve yet to catch onto whatever sort of vibes Maya used to pick up on that made her aware of their approach, I imagine we’re getting close to another based on the time-frame alone.
: Taking that into consideration and measuring it against the other apocalypses I’ve gone through, I can only assume the next one might happen any day now.
scene ayanepresentation24
: And that means we need to act sooner rather than later if we want to make any progress this time around.

: Sensei, you’re probably not aware of this since you and Ami have both been away from school for a while, but our next beach trip is tomorrow. And I want you to come. But I want you to come without Ami.
: That’s...probably a little easier said than done.
: I’m sure you’ll figure it out. And, in the event that you’re uncomfortable being around the entire class at once again, don’t be. Because I’m already working on a plan for that as well.
: Question — why does it need to be during the beach trip? Do these apocalypses always occur during class gatherings, or-
scene ayanepresentation25
: I’m glad you asked, Makoto! Because this is where phase one of my foolproof plan comes into play!

: We are but young girls, oblivious to the ways of the world! But what we do know is how to create a vast network of information and different methods of exchanging it! And the best method of all, you ask?
scene ayanepresentation26
: We throw a slumber party!
scene ayanepresentation27
: That’s phase one of your plan to “save the world?” A slumber party?
: Not just any slumber party! A beach slumber party in Sensei’s room at the inn! Super secret and invite-only, just like the last time we did this.
: You’ve used this method before?
: Yes and, if I’m remembering correctly, it immediately invoked an apocalypse.
: That it did, Sensei. Which means it’s very possible that it happens again.
: Sure. But last time, I had a little more of an opportunity to get Yumi and Tsuneyo to agree. I have no idea how I’d manage that on such short notice this time.
: Leave all of that to me, Sensei! You just worry about a way to keep Ami at home and make it so you can come to the party without her. Because I love Ami, but all she’d do here is get in the way.
: And what do I do?
: Just show up, I guess. I didn’t really factor you into the equation since I wasn’t positive you were even going to make it here today.
scene ayanepresentation28
: Yeah, I probably wouldn’t have if you didn’t show up at my house with your butler.
: So...I just worry about getting to the beach alone-
: And we throw a midnight bash where we poke and prod at our classmates’ minds with apocalyptic info to see if anything sticks!
: It’s not foolproof by any means. But we’re running out of time, and it’s way easier to get everyone together when we’re already...you know...together.
: If that’s...what you think is best.
scene ayanepresentation29

: How do you feel, though? Are you really ready to start doing things like this again? Because I was under the impression you were trying to just...remove yourself from the class atmosphere altogether.
: Frankly? I’m not ready. And I’m not looking forward to it at all.
scene ayanepresentation30
: But I trust Ayane...so I’m going to put all my faith in her since I have nowhere else to put it now.
scene ayanepresentation31
: Thank you, Sensei...
: I know I’m no Maya, but I’m going to do my best.
scene ayanepresentation32
: And honestly? Doing my best is way easier when she’s not here to doubt me all the time. Like seriously, what the fuck was that about?
: I mean, if I was an immortal time-traveler, which I guess I kind of...am now?...I’d doubt you too if your first plan was throwing a slumber party.
: The slumber party method has worked 100%% of the time. Kind of. It’s foolproof. Mostly.
: Also, it’ll be fun sneaking into Sensei’s bed while everyone else is asleep and reclaiming his body as mine.
scene black
: Note to self — wear earplugs to bed.
: Earplugs will be provided to all attendees free-of-charge! Except Sensei. I want him to hear me.
: Okay. I’m going to head home now if that’s all we’re doing today.
: Wait, Dad-
: Dad?
: Don’t worry, I’ve got a plan for Ami. Just call me tomorrow when the coast is clear for me to head over.
: Got it. I love you! Makoto, do you need a ride? Geoffrey’s probably in his cryo-chamber right now, but I can page him if you-
: I’ll walk home with Sensei, it’s fine.
: I’d rather be alone right now, actually. But I’ll see you tomorrow night, Makoto.
: Ugh...fine. Also, cryo-chamber?
: Oh, yeah. Geoffrey is actually-
I leave the Amamiya mansion and...try to snap myself into whatever state of mind will allow me to pretend things are normal again.
scene nightsky
I spend the rest of the day by Ami’s side.
It’s the least I can do since I’ll be leaving her tomorrow.
But it’ll also be a good opportunity.
Not for me, but for her.
And for the girl who volunteered to stay by her side.
scene black
I think I’ll be ready to have a talk soon.
